title: Your Life as an Undercover Agent at Every Level (Not Even Yours)
hook: The gun's warm against your temple. One wrong word and this alley keeps your body. You're not a made man. You're the fed about to disappear into the man you were sent to destroy.
body: POV: a composite FBI Special Agent who rises through the real, documented Bureau ladder — New Agent Trainee (21 weeks at Quantico) to Special Agent, First Office of Assignment, to Certified Undercover Employee (the real designation, cleared for sensitive 'Group I' operations under DOJ's Attorney General's Guidelines) to a years-long deep-cover placement inside an organized-crime crew, to case agent wearing the wire, to Supervisory Special Agent, to Assistant/Special Agent in Charge, to the Bureau's own oversight above you. Real, verified mechanics woven in: the GS pay scale plus the mandatory 25% Law Enforcement Availability Pay every Special Agent receives regardless of assignment; the federal statute (5 U.S.C. §8335) forcing every agent, any rank, into retirement at exactly age 57; and the documented psychological toll undercover work takes on marriages and identity. Joseph D. Pistone's real six-year 'Donnie Brasco' infiltration of the Bonanno crime family is referenced only as real background grounding for the genre's stakes — this episode's protagonist, mentor, target, and rival are a FICTIONAL COMPOSITE; no real living person is depicted. Watch the whole series — every life, every level, every name you have to give up to climb. For educational and entertainment purposes.
pinned: Real fact: a Certified Undercover Employee gets paid on the exact same GS pay scale as a desk analyst down the hall — no extra 'danger money' for becoming someone else for years at a time. Which level do you think costs the most: the first lie, or the last one?
poll: Which level costs the most? LEVEL 03 (the ring comes off, Ray Cole doesn't wear one) / LEVEL 04 (the birthday dinner — you like the man you're built to destroy) / LEVEL 05 (the dock, the gun, the wire under your ribs) / LEVEL 08 (retirement at 57 — the one number the Bureau controls, not you)
